answer: Autonomous rovers on a glacier resist Sybil attacks through spatial optical attestation. A base station directs pulsed laser challenges via a fast-steering mirror, validating the round-trip delay and bearing of each responder. An attacker cannot forge identities digitally and must deploy discrete physical transceivers at distinct geographic coordinates. However, severe blizzards and thermal turbulence cause beam paths to wander, intermittently rejecting authentic agents.
